Gather evidence` names: it declines correctly at conflict_resolution — naming c_001 and routing to conflict-resolution — but reports `repository_breadth` met without the registration start date that decides it. #2529 (from issue #2269) rewrote that step to bind the fetch to its consumers ("call `wiki_read` … and do not begin Step 2 until it has returned or failed"). Probed against that fixed agent on 2026-09-14: the routed original ut_research_exhaustiveness_009 now PASSES and makes the call; this twin still fails and still makes no call. So the binding took on the routed route and not on the direct one under an adversarial delegation — which is the asymmetry this arm exists to surface, and the reason the marker stays. FLAKY, NOT DETERMINISTIC — the agent fetches on a minority of runs, so an `xpass` is expected and is NOT evidence the defect is fixed; do not remove this marker on the strength of one green run. Remove it when the direct route fetches on the declining path; the agent-body work belongs to issue #2269.

The skill must decline to declare exhaustive, naming the unresolved conflict as the specific blocker rather than a general "not yet."

judge_context: The conflict_resolution stop criterion explicitly states that all discrepancies must be resolved before a declaration is valid unresolved conflicts block proof. This test checks whether Claude applies that criterion rather than declaring based on the weight of supporting evidence alone. Strong evidence in favor of a conclusion is not the same as having resolved every contradiction, and Claude should distinguish the two. The failure mode is Claude declaring exhaustive while treating the conflict as minor or already settled, or never mentioning it at all. A correct response keeps declared as false and names the unresolved conflict as the specific gap, not just a vague "more work needed."
